column1: # tests/coverage-floor.tsv - Q11: coverage may not go down.
# One row per file the host tier builds: the line-coverage percentage
# below which `make coverage-check` fails. Raised by hand, with the
# commit that raised it, exactly like tests/budgets.tsv - and lowered by
# hand too, because deleting a test can be the right call and should have
# to be said out loud rather than happening quietly.
# Q8 deliberately set no coverage *target*, and that still stands: the
# absolute number is whatever the tests honestly reach. This constrains
# only the direction.
# A caveat worth carrying next to these numbers: line coverage is the
# weaker of the two instruments here. `net/ethernet.c` sat at 100% lines
# with a **0%** mutation score until Q12 looked - every line ran and
# nothing asserted what any of them did. Read this file next to
# `make mutate`, never instead of it.
# M101: the names here are repo-relative paths, and they used to be
# relative to kernel/ instead. llvm-cov prints each file with the longest
# common prefix of everything on its command line removed, so adding the
# first user-space source to the report shortened nothing and lengthened
# every kernel name. Every floor in this file stopped matching, and the
# ratchet reported ten "new" files and "nothing fell" - which is a
# ratchet that has quietly stopped ratcheting. tools/coverage-ratchet.py
# now fails when a name in this file is absent from the report, so the
# next time that happens it is an error rather than a silence.
# M100: the floors are the MEASURED number now, not a round number under
# it, and every file in the report has one.
# Both changes are the same repair. Rounding 83.82 down to 83 meant the
# ratchet printed "raised ... raise it, and say so" for seven files on
# every run, forever, and eight more files had no row at all and printed
# "new" on every run. Fifteen lines of advice nobody was going to act on,
# on every single run - and underneath them, two floors that had actually
# FALLEN and had been falling since M98. The noise is what hid them.
# So: exact values, and tools/coverage-ratchet.py now fails on a file
# with no row rather than printing one more line. The report should be
# silent when nothing changed, because that is the only state in which
# anybody reads it.
# file<TAB>line_coverage_floor<TAB>commit<TAB>note
kernel/lib/libk.c
column4: Every line. Mutation score 73.8%, which is the more interesting number.

column4: Mutation score 89.4% after Q12's split and coalescing tests.

column1: kernel/net/ip.c

column1: kernel/net/icmp.c
column4: M100: exact rather than 74. Mutation score 59.4%; the unreachable part is the error-message paths.

column1: kernel/net/udp.c
column4: M100: exact rather than 96. Was 28% before Q12's checksum tests. Mutation score 80.5%.

column1: kernel/net/ethernet.c
column4: Was 90% lines at a 0% mutation score - the file that proved why this table is not enough on its own.

column1: kernel/net/tcp.c
column4: M100: exact rather than 62. Was 3.74% and the largest hole in the suite from Q8 until Q11. tests/test_tcp_states.c drives the eleven-state machine one segment at a time and found two remotely-triggerable defects on its first run.

column1: kernel/dev/fwcfg.c
column4: M100: 89.55% until M100, and under this floor since M98 - three fw_cfg switches were added (bootstrap, pytest, pybuild) and the test that exists to catch a shared cache between them was grown for the first two and not the third. Its own comment had warned about exactly that, three lines above the table it needed a row in. 100% now: the switch table in tests/test_fwcfg.c is derived from one array, every switch is asked on every case, and each is asked twice.

column1: user_space/lib/symtab.c
column4: M100: exact rather than 97. M101: the profile report's symbol resolver, and the first user-space file in this tier. The two uncovered lines are the guards for a symbol file that is not ascending, which the parser cannot produce and only a hand-written one can. Four hand-run mutations against its tests were all caught, which is the number that matters more than this one.

column1: kernel/dev/random.c
column4: M100: the entropy source, ChaCha20 (RFC 7539) under a fast-key-erasure pool. The uncovered lines are the RDRAND/RDSEED path, which is #if'd out under LEANOS_HOST_TEST because the host test cannot hold a hardware generator still - graded on the machine by the [rng] marker instead, and by tests/test_random.c against the RFC vector for everything the host can reach.

column1: kernel/fs/flock.c
column4: M100: first floor. POSIX record locks, the table sqlite's transactions take three of. The one uncovered line is claim()'s NULL return, which flock_set makes unreachable by counting free entries first - and the mutation harness agrees, its one survivor there being that return. Mutation score 91.5%; the other nine survivors are `<` to `<=` on the table's loop bounds, a one-past-the-end read that only a sanitizer sees and the campaign runs without one.

column1: kernel/dev/pty.c
column4: M100: first floor. M85's pseudo-terminals, every line reached by tests/test_pty.c.

column1: kernel/dev/tty.c
column4: M100: first floor. The line discipline - canonical and raw modes, signals, job control. The uncovered part is the paths that need a real framebuffer console under them.

column1: kernel/sched/sched.c
column4: M118: 49.86 -> 50.40, and the raise is claimed here because it is this milestone's: fd_release and fd_retain grew an FD_UNIX case each and tests/test_unixsock.c drives both. M100: first floor, and the most overdue row in this file. 2,157 lines, in the host tier since Q13 against a fake timer and a fake CPU, and until M100 nothing constrained its direction at all - it printed "new" on every run for as long as nobody read past the summary. Half the file is the multi-core and signal-delivery paths that Q13's harness does not drive yet; raising this is the measurable half of the queue's row 5.

column1: user_space/libc/src/errno.c
column4: M100: first floor. One line, and M99 is the milestone that proved it matters - five syscalls returned -1 over an untouched errno and the visible symptom was print() writing nothing and exiting 0.

column1: user_space/libc/src/fnmatch.c
column4: M100: first floor. The uncovered part is the character-class names inside bracket expressions.

column1: user_space/libc/src/getopt.c
column4: M100: first floor.

column1: user_space/libc/src/libgen.c
column4: M100: first floor. dirname and basename, both entirely reached.

column1: user_space/libc/src/wchar.c
column4: M117: 48.50 -> 48.24. Not a test removed: `make coverage` had not compiled since M111 (its CFLAGS lacked -Iuser_space/lib and -DLEANOS_HOST_TEST, which every other host build has), and with them wchar.c compiles three lines the tests never reached. M100: first floor, and the honest number for a file that exists because GNU hello's first line asked for it (M94). Half of it is the wide stdio family, which nothing in the host tier calls.

column1: kernel/drivers/rtl8139_ring.c
column4: M117: first floor, set where M116's test left it - the ring model against every frame length.

column1: user_space/lib/dns.c
column4: M117: first floor, set where the M114 resolver tests left it.

column1: user_space/lib/fsutil.c
column4: M117: first floor, set where M112's tree-walk tests left it.

column1: user_space/lib/ospkg.c
column4: M117: first floor, set where M111's package tests left it.

column1: user_space/lib/sha256.c
column4: M117: first floor - the differential test against the host reaches every line.

column1: user_space/libc/src/wallclock.c
column4: M117: first floor - M116's four tests at every phase reach every line.

column1: kernel/ipc/unixsock.c
column4: M118: first floor. AF_UNIX and SCM_RIGHTS. The uncovered lines are the paths that need a heap failure (kmalloc returning NULL in unix_new) and the ring's two-chunk wraparound on a message that straddles the end of the buffer, which needs a 4 KiB-scale fixture rather than the short strings these tests use. Mutation score 87.2%; of the five survivors, three are equivalent mutations and two are one-past-the-end reads that only a sanitizer sees - and the campaign runs without one.
